resources.string: Reachable from the tailnet

Off, a proxy here serves only this device. On, every device of your tailnet the access rules allow can use it at this device\'s tailnet address. Remote management, Taildrop, Taildrive folders and Serve do not need these switches.

Right now the native TUN engine carries the tailnet, and TailSocks itself is outside that VPN: the tailnet reaches none of these proxies, open or not. These switches work in proxy mode and with the hev engine.

Right now Root Mode\'s interface carries the tailnet: what listens on every address (local network access) is reached from the tailnet anyway, and nothing else is. These switches work in proxy mode and with the hev engine.
SOCKS5 from the tailnet
When open, it lets other devices of your tailnet into this device\'s local network and out to the internet as this device.
HTTP proxy from the tailnet
When open, it lets other devices of your tailnet into this device\'s local network and out to the internet as this device. It never asks for a password.
DNS proxy from the tailnet
When open, other devices of your tailnet can look up names through this device, MagicDNS and split DNS names included.
Taildrive proxy from the tailnet
When open, other devices of your tailnet can open the Taildrive folders this device may open, as this device.
This device only.
Open at %1$s.
Open on port %1$s of this device\'s tailnet address.
The proxy is off.
It listens on %1$s, where the tailnet cannot be let in: 127.0.0.1 can.
In this mode the tailnet does not reach it.
In this mode the tailnet reaches it through local network access, whatever this switch says.
The SOCKS5 proxy has no username or password: every device of your tailnet the access rules allow can use it.
Set a password
The Taildrive proxy asks for no login: every device of your tailnet the access rules allow can open your Taildrive folders through it. Turn the login on in Taildrive\'s settings.
Open SOCKS5 to the tailnet?

It has no username or password. Any device of your tailnet the access rules allow could use this device as a way into its local network and out to the internet. Set a password first and give it only to the devices that should use the proxy.
